result.line: E3b: minimum total Lucas defect on k = 5 shared-quadratic-A Korselt families f_1 = 1 + cA, f_j = 1 + l_j A (x - r_j) (j = 2..5), A = x^2 + px + q, deg F = 14, moduli dim 5
result.outcome: KILL in the numerical sense, not as a theorem. No family with total Lucas defect <= 7 was found; the minimum appears to be 8 (total gcd Sum m = 6). It is attained only at isolated algebraic points, and none of those is defined over Q. The conjectured minimum 7 = deg F/2 is not attained. Every exact Groebner route (over Q and over F_p) timed out, so the 'minimum = 7' theorem was NOT obtained. What is proved: four structural lemmas and an arithmetic-genus computation that explains the intractability.
claims: PROVED (Lemma A, Lucas reduction, any odd k). Let N_j = f_j + 1 = 2 + A g_j and Phi_j = prod_{i != j}(g_j - 2 g_i) - g_j^(k-1). Then g_j^(k-1)(F+1) == -Phi_j mod N_j and gcd(g_j, N_j) = 1, so deg gcd(F+1, f_j+1) = deg gcd(N_j, Phi_j) with multiplicities. Phi_j depends only on the g's. Korselt_j <=> K_j(A(r_j)) = 0 with K_j(a) = [prod_{i != j}(1 + a g_i(r_j)) - 1]/a, which covers A(r_j) = 0 too. Equivalently, with H = (F-1)/A: Lucas at theta <=> H(theta) = g_j(theta), and Korselt <=> H(r_j) = 0 = g_j(r_j).

PROVED (Lemma B, FSP). If f_j(t) = -1 for all j, then F(t) = (-1)^k = -1, so t is a Lucas point of every member (k odd). This costs k - 1 conditions and gives Sum m >= k. With A = x^2 - 1 and E_i(x) = (x^2-1)(x - r_i), the FSP families are f_1 = 1 - 2(x^2-1)/(t^2-1) and f_i = 1 - 2E_i(x)/E_i(t). f_1 is full on FSP <=> prod(3t + r_i) = prod(t - r_i). The extra Lucas points of member j are x = t*sigma with sigma^2 + u_j*sigma + u_j = 1/T, where T = t^2 and u_i = (t - r_i)/t. A family is defined over Q iff T and all u_i are rational.

PROVED (Lemma C, parity). Take a family invariant as a set under the reflection of x about the vertex of A. The reflection fixes f_1 and pairs the cubics fixed-point-freely, so m_3 = m_2 and m_5 = m_4. m_1 is even: gcd(N_1, Phi_1) of two reflection-even polynomials is even or odd, and the odd case would need x || gcd, but x | N_1 forces N_1 = 2x^2 and then x^2 divides both. Hence Sum m is even on this locus.

PROVED (Lemma E). A Lucas point of member j is never another member's Korselt root r_i: Korselt at r_i forces prod_{l != i,j} f_l(r_i) = -1, while Lucas at r_i would need it to be +1. A Lucas point is also never a root of A, since N_j = 2 there.

PROVED (adjunction; arithmetic genus, assuming the expected dimension). For fixed (A, r_2..r_5), the Korselt conditions cut a complete intersection of 4 multilinear hypersurfaces in (P^1)^5 (c, l_2..l_5) of arithmetic genus 32. The same computation gives genus 0 for k = 3, consistent with E3's rational 3-fold. This is why the k = 5 Korselt variety has no evident rational parametrisation and plain Groebner stalls.

HEURISTIC (naive dimension count). The Korselt moduli are 5-dimensional. Each Lucas node, shared or not, costs exactly as many conditions as it adds to Sum m, except a node shared by all five members (FSP), which gains 1. So the expected maximum is Sum m = 6 at dimension 0. The two observed mechanisms reaching 6 (FSP + 1 incidence, and reflection symmetry with 3 paired conditions) are exactly at this count, with no further excess.

COMPUTED (numerical survey, NOT a proof). For k = 5, max Sum m = 6, so the minimum total Lucas defect is 8. No Sum m = 7 point was found in any of the 13 gcd patterns, the 397 incidence structures, the FSP sublocus, or the symmetric locus (Sum m = 8 patterns). Since Sum m >= 8 strata lie inside Sum m = 7 strata, this also covers all larger totals.

COMPUTED (numerical). The conjectured equality 'minimum = 7 = deg F/2' is not supported for k = 5: no defect-7 family exists in the surveyed strata. The half-defect inequality (defect >= 7) holds with slack.

COMPUTED (numerical). Every defect-8 minimiser found is an isolated point of one of six types: FSP + f_1 full (~66 points); FSP + one cubic member's second Lucas point (~239); symmetric (2,1,1,1,1), (2,2,2,0,0), (0,2,2,1,1), and (0,3,3,0,0) (complex only). Lucas points: FSP types have t for all members plus -t (member 1) or s (member j); symmetric types have +-w for member 1 and mirror pairs theta, -theta for members 2/3 and 4/5.
COMPUTED (bounded-height/degree test). No real minimiser is defined over Q, so no defect-8 family has integer specialisations. There was nothing to scan and no candidate n to test with src/bpsw.py.
COMPUTED (calibration). The same numerical machinery at k = 3 reproduces E3: rho-family at dim 1 with f_1 full automatic on the FSP locus, P23, and no Sum m = 5.
HEURISTIC (k = 3 and 5 data). Max Sum m = k + 1, i.e. min defect 2k - 2. This equals deg F/2 = (3k-1)/2 only at k = 3, which explains the E3 coincidence that motivated the conjecture.
HEURISTIC. The line cannot beat rho: relative defect 8/14 = 0.571 versus 4/8 = 0.5. Even a defect-7 family would only tie.

(2) pkill -f was used once; it matched only my own processes but killed my ssh session. All later stops were kill <pid>. (3) All compute ran on dirichlet within the 2-core budget, apart from one brief third process that I stopped by pid.

(2) Recall: the outcome rests on random-start searches of overdetermined systems, and these have ZERO demonstrated recall on known non-empty excess structures. node_model gets 0/30000 on 1|1|2|2|3|3, which does contain the symmetric (2,2,2,0,0) points; E3b's own node6.log shows 0/4000. result.line: HD (half-defect inequality): sum_j (deg(f_j+1) - deg gcd(F+1, f_j+1)) >= deg F / 2 for real Korselt families, k odd >= 3
result.outcome: HD is REFUTED for every odd k >= 5, including families whose leading coefficients are all positive. The counterexamples are linear Korselt families sharing a common root, and composing them with any polynomial u gives counterexamples at every degree. In these families the total defect is exactly 2*deg u = 2D/k, so no bound of the form defect >= c*D (c > 0 fixed) can hold. In particular the D/4 variant fails for k >= 9. For k = 3, HD survives every test and is proved on several infinite strata. It is not proved in general. Best partial theorems: (i) C-lemma: a linear family with a common root has at least 2 Lucas-dead members, over any field of characteristic 0; this is sharp for every k. (ii) A-reduction lemma: the Lucas-good part does not depend on the common factor A, so HD holds whenever A is large. (iii) Sweep lemma: the Korselt-only version of Lemma 6, giving defect >= 1 (>= 2 under conditions) whenever a non-simultaneous real special point exists. Replacement conjecture: defect >= 2*d_min. It is attained with equality by the doubling-chain compositions and by the rho-family, and it would imply that no real Williams family exists. No BPSW candidate n arose, because these are real or mixed-sign polynomial families.
